name: whisper-cpp
description: whisper.cpp's ggml CPU backend -- the same kai_run_matmul_*/KleidiAI question as llama-cpp-kleidiai, asked of a sibling ggml-based project that ships its OWN CPU backend build (not llama.cpp's), and that (unlike llama.cpp in this repo's builds) dynamically dlopen's its backend and logs the fact.
why_it_matters: whisper.cpp shares ggml with llama.cpp but is packaged and built independently (its own CMake flags, its own release process, its own Homebrew/distro formula) -- KleidiAI being on in one does not imply anything about the other. This preset also demonstrates a mechanism the kleidiai/cpu-variants presets never exercise: newer ggml builds (GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON, the mechanism this Homebrew formula uses) print a real 'load_backend: loaded CPU backend from <path>' line at startup -- a genuine, generalizable L2 signal for which backend .so got loaded, independent of KleidiAI-specific log lines.

l1.note: Same regex/family order as llama-cpp-kleidiai -- same ggml KleidiAI integration, different project's build. A Homebrew-installed whisper-cpp's CPU backend lib is NOT next to the whisper-cli binary (it lives in the separate `ggml` formula's keg, e.g. /opt/homebrew/Cellar/ggml/<version>/libexec/libggml-cpu.so) -- lib_globs above cover a same-directory (source-build) layout; for a Homebrew install, pass --lib-name explicitly (see verified_against) or --lib-dir pointed at the ggml keg's libexec/.

l2.note: 'load_backend_cpu' is the signal actually expected to fire on a GGML_BACKEND_DL build (verified below); 'advertised_family' mirrors llama-cpp-kleidiai's pattern for a source build with KleidiAI on, but is NOT expected to fire on the stock Homebrew formula (no --enable-kleidiai-style flag in that formula as of this check -- see verified_against).

l3.note: Same fail-closed breakpoint mechanism as llama-cpp-kleidiai. On the stock Homebrew build (0 kai_ symbols, see l1), run_target_check()'s pre-flight enumerate_dispatch_symbols() guard correctly refuses to launch an uninstrumented probe -- verified below. A from-source whisper.cpp build with -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON should be expected to behave like llama-cpp-kleidiai's L3 (real, non-zero hits), but that specific positive case has not been built/tested here (see caveats).

workload.note: whisper-cli --help needs no model/audio file and still exercises backend loading + prints system_info (confirmed below) -- a genuinely lower-friction smoke check than llama-cli's workload, which requires a real .gguf. A full transcription workload (`-m ggml-base.bin -f audio.wav`) would additionally exercise L3 with real inference if run against a build that actually has kai_run_matmul symbols; not required for --help-only L1/L2 verification.

verified_against.artifact: Homebrew whisper-cpp 1.9.2 (bottled) + its `ggml` formula dependency 0.18.1, bin/whisper-cli + libexec/libggml-cpu.so
verified_against.result: `polygraph check whisper-cpp --binary .../whisper-cli --lib-name .../ggml/0.18.1/libexec/libggml-cpu.so` (run for real, --help workload, no model needed): L1: 0/0 kai_-prefixed symbols (this formula is not built with KleidiAI; a separate, unfiltered nm count independently found 403 total exported symbols in the same lib, zero of them kai_-prefixed). L2: load_backend_cpu matched with value '/Users/.../ggml/0.18.1/libexec/libggml-cpu.so' -- confirms the GGML_BACKEND_DL log line is real and this preset's regex for it is correct; advertised_family did not match (expected, no KleidiAI). L3: enumerate_dispatch_symbols() found 0 candidates and run_target_check() correctly refused to launch lldb (error 'no symbols matching ... refusing to run an uninstrumented probe'), matching L1's 0-symbol finding rather than reporting a misleading L3 pass or a silent 0 -- verdict L3_UNAVAILABLE, exit 2, not a false 0-and-fine.

caveats: The positive-dispatch case (a whisper.cpp build WITH KleidiAI compiled in, producing real non-zero L3 hits the way llama-cpp-kleidiai's verified_against does) was not built or tested here -- only the stock Homebrew formula (KleidiAI off) was available. The regex/mechanism is identical to llama-cpp-kleidiai's, which IS verified positive, so this is a low-risk gap, but it is a gap.

Homebrew's multi-keg layout (whisper-cli in one Cellar path, libggml-cpu.so in a separate `ggml` formula's keg) means the auto-relative lib_globs will not find the lib without --lib-name/--lib-dir on a Homebrew install specifically; a self-built or official-tarball layout (bin/+lib/ side by side, matching llama.cpp's) would resolve automatically.
